title: Who played at the gallery that night; the judge's lecture
summary: Punch and Allen reconstruct the band members present and tell what the judge said.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I remember that. You remember? Yeah, but the judge don't order them to explain it.
Yeah. Well let's see, who was there? In the band? Yeah. Yeah.
There was one. And wasn't that the fella who used to play the sticks?
He didn't have no drums. The guy you have a picture of at home?
Yeah, he was there.
Fergie, yeah. That was Ferguson. And Charlie DeVoe. Yeah, and then they had the banjo player from Wisconsin.
Yeah. Joe Oltzalter and his Brady. And Kit Thomas. Yeah. He asked Kit Thomas a lot of questions.
And he knew Kit Thomas. Yeah, you know better than that, don't you?
Yeah. Boy, that was funny, I'm telling you in a way.
And they had that drummer named Doggy.
I can't remember.
He was there.
He was there.

Yeah. Well, I mean, Dick, where you was that night?
I had a headache.
I always know you'll always be there, you know.

Well, that night I just didn't feel like coming. I don't know. I couldn't get with it, you know. I had a headache. Uh-huh. But I got away. I always miss it so far. They never had to take me to the jailhouse. Yeah. Well, he wasn't taking me.
He said he'd never seen this thing before in his life.
Well, they didn't take Erwin in. I believe they did.
Or he got out of there or something.
I don't know. You know who was playing? Joe Lodd was playing piano that night. And he didn't have any horn with him, you know. He wasn't playing trumpet.
Oh, yeah.
Yeah. And he just walked out. They couldn't catch him, you know. Yeah. Joe told me about that.
I think the only white boy was with us in that coat was Charlie. Charlie, wasn't it Charlie?
Charlie and the two boys.
Yeah, two more boys.
Two boys from Wisconsin. Yeah. Joel Salter and Doggy. I think Doggy's name was Burger. And they, let's see, they had Ewan, Eddie Morris, and Kent Thomas.
Yeah.
And I missed that lecture from the judge myself. I wasn't there.

Boy, he did some talking. He told Ewan, say, what you people doing up there? You can't do it here. He said, they're trying to do it to us, but before, the only way they do it, they got to ram it down our throats. I don't need this now, no. I shouldn't take it. I just take so much medicine. I always want to take something. There ain't nothing bothering me now. I ain't going to take it. Let me sit there. Okay.
Well, you do need it.
Yeah. And that's the way that come off.
